raw_response:
I would keep my year simple and spread my risk instead of pushing all 16.1 mu into one thing. I only have 3 years of farming experience and primary-school education, so I would choose a plan I can manage with my family labor and with the well water I already have. I would still lean on eggplant as my main cash crop because that is my cropping system, but I would not put everything into it. I would keep some wheat and maize for steady grain output and use cabbage and cauliflower to bring in cash at different times. I would use hybrid seed on eggplant, cabbage, cauliflower, and maize because I want more stable emergence and yield, and I would keep wheat as improved seed because it is reliable and easier for me to manage. I would use plough tillage for wheat and maize, and mostly rotary tillage for vegetables because it is faster and suits intensive planting better. Since I have well irrigation, I would irrigate vegetables more often and grain less often. I would keep fertilizer moderate, not extreme, because I want yield but I also want to avoid wasting money and creating too much pest pressure. I would expect eggplant to get the most water, fertilizer, and spraying because it stays in the field longer and earns more, while wheat and maize would be managed more steadily and cheaply.
